ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus collegalensis* (Gekkonidae) reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark brown dorsal crossbands and scattered white spots. Distinguishing features include a slender body and granular scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus collegalensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale nuchal collar and a series of dark, paired vertebral spots along its back.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus collegalensis* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky scrublands in peninsular India, typically found at low to moderate elevations among boulders and trees.
ai.behavior: The Forest Spotted Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and invertebrates on tree trunks and rocky surfaces within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus collegalensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus collegalensis* is found in the dry forests of southern India, specifically across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh, up to 1,000m elevation.
